When you widen\n> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same\n> commit, per `meta.md` §5.\n\nThe `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant \"the\nworkflow file changed, so re-run everything\"; locally the workflow layer is a\nwhole tree — the frozen reference `pr-ci.yml`, every driver and helper under\n`local/bin/`, every protocol under `local/protocols/`, and the hooks in\n`.githooks/` — and a change to any of them forces a full run, every step\nincluded. The globs are that broad on purpose: a `gh_common.py`-only change has\nto run the `scripts/tests` unit suite that covers it — carried by\n`blueprint-sync` — and under the old three-file glob such a change matched no\narea and ran nothing at all (PR 7 review, F13).\n\n## 4. Manifest schema\n\nBuilt in runtime storage (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) and then\nposted as the manifest PR comment (§5):\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.json          complete run\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<pr>-<head_sha>.partial.json  partial run\n```\n\nA run is **partial** when it was given `--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`;\n`--dry-run` writes nothing at all.\n\nStep logs live outside the repository, under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"schema\": 1,\n  \"generator\": \"local/bin/ci.sh\",\n  \"replaces\": \".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml\",\n  \"pr\": 7,                       // GitHub PR number\n  \"branch\": \"issue-7-qpbt-basis\",\n  \"base\": \"main\",                // from the GitHub PR\n  \"base_ref\": \"origin/main\",     // what actually resolved\n  \"merge_base\": \"<sha>\",\n  \"head_sha\": \"<sha>\",           // the SHA every step ran against\n  \"worktree\": \"/abs/path\",\n  \"started\": \"2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800\",   // ISO-8601 with offset\n  \"finished\": \"2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800\",\n  \"seconds\": 1125,               // whole run, integer\n  \"conclusion\": \"success\",       // success | failure | error\n  \"partial\": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict\n  \"areas\": { \"lean\": true, \"blueprint_src\": false, ... },\n  \"changed_files\": [\"MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean\", ...],\n  \"warnings\": [\"texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...\", ...],\n  \"steps\": [\n    {\n      \"step\": \"build\",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight\n      \"outcome\": \"success\",      // success | failure | error | skipped\n      \"seconds\": 883,\n      \"log_path\": \"/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log\",\n      \"blocking\": true,\n      \"note\": \"\"                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nOutcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:\n\n| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |\n|---|---|---|\n| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |\n| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |\n| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |\n| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |\n\n`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,\nelse `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == \"success\"`.\n\n## 5. Publication\n\nEvidence goes to GitHub, bound to the exact SHA the steps ran against\n(`issues-prs.md` §2). For every complete run:\n\n* one `local-ci/<step>` status per gate step — `pending` posted before the\n  step, then `success | failure | error`; a gated-out step is a `success`\n  whose description says it was skipped, so the gate never has to distinguish\n  \"absent\" from \"not applicable\";\n* `local-ci/summary` carrying the run's `conclusion`;\n* the manifest JSON as the PR comment marked\n  `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, created or updated in place.\n\n`pending` before the first step is the old `ci_status: running`: a crashed,\nkilled or power-cut run leaves `pending`, never a stale `success`, so the\nreview gate's \"green CI on the same head SHA\" check (invariant 2) fails closed.\nImmediately before the final publication `ci.sh` re-reads both the local branch\ntip and the remote PR head; if either moved, it publishes no success and exits\nnonzero, because a status is a claim about one commit.\n\nA **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`, or `--base`) publishes nothing at\nall — no statuses, no manifest comment — and keeps its manifest in runtime\nstorage only. `--base` belongs on that list because an overridden base (the PR\nhead, say) can empty the diff and mark every gate skipped-success. Partial runs\nare a debugging aid; they must not be able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and\nthey must not clobber a complete manifest for the same SHA.\n\n## 6. Concurrency and locks\n\nTwo advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under\n`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each\nholds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its\nowner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`\n(default 3 h).\n\n| Lock | Scope | On contention |\n|---|---|---|\n| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |\n| `$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |\n\nOnly the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and\ntake nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and\ntake nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them\nper-file without serializing.\n\n`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs\n(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —\nthe ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:\nkilling a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.\nSo a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is\nwaited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove\nthe lease directories by hand.\n\n## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache\n\n`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the\nshared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save\npolicy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of\n~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,\nso no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a\nworktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.\n\n1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,\n   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:\n   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a\n   hard error.\n   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);\n     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.\n2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and\n   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never\n   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main\n   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,\n   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`\n   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run\n   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.\n3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at\n   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets\n   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that\n   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know\n   is clean.\n4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the\n   comparator drift check.\n\nEvery `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets\n`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`\nmake Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;\n`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any\norchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.\n\nLake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot\nolder than the merge base is safe — but only within one\n`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that\nboundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates\nthe check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.\n\n## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run\n\n`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by\nrepeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a\nhuman to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is\ndifferent but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build\nbudget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and\nwhen it answers `true` the run records a warning:\n\n> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment\n\nDe-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and\nthis one is inherited rather than invented.\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nWhen `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:\n\n```json\n{\"ts\":\"…\",\"kind\":\"ci-build\",\"trigger\":\"ci.sh pr=0007\",\"seconds\":883,\n \"outcome\":\"success\",\"sha\":\"…\",\"note\":\"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis\"}\n```\n\nThis satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and\nmakes \"how much wall time did CI cost this PR\" answerable by a script. The\nper-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.\n\n## 10. Trust boundary\n\nTwo things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.\n\n**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and\n`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI\nmeans and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would\nnot run a shell script from.\n\n**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test\nfailures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.\n`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer\nthat feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the\nsanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,\ntruncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest\ngives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the\nconsumer's explicit, visible responsibility.\n\n## 11. Amendments\n\nChanging a gating glob, a step's command set, the manifest schema, the status\ncontexts or their vocabulary, or a lock's name or semantics is an amendment:\nrecord the trigger in `results/telemetry/events.md`, edit this file and\n`ci.sh` together, append to `EVOLUTION.md`, and grep `local/` for every other\nenforcement point (`meta.md` §5). The manifest schema in particular is a\ncontract with `review.sh`, `autofix.sh` and `pr_merge.py`; bump `schema` when\nit changes incompatibly.\n# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache\n\nNormative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent\nworkflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to\navoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:\n\n| script | role |\n|---|---|\n| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |\n| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |\n| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |\n\nGoverning invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full\n`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,\n`DESIGN.md` wins.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way\n\nThe parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented\nfailure. `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *\"after repeated runner disk exhaustion\"* |\n\nThe single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable\ncache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the\nsame failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared\nbuild tree.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The two-tier split\n\n`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and\ndifferent sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the\nparent's failure.\n\nAn absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a\none-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and\ncanonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,\nplus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or\nwarming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.\n\n**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,\n`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the\nparent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and\ndistributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**\ncopy.\n\n**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The\nparent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud\ncache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once\nper manifest** in a shared, read-only store:\n`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,\nand every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.\n\n> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a\n> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it\n> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any\n> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest\n> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by\n> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old\n> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches\n> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,\n> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key\n> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).\n> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.\n\nConsequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It\nrewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under\nevery published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib\nbumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.\n\n---\n\n## 3. The cache key\n\n```\nkeyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )\n```\n\nconcatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local\nanalog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in\n`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`\nand `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay\nbyte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.\nA missing input file is a hard error, never a default.\n\nTwo properties matter, and they are not symmetric:\n\n1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's\n   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest\n   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is\n   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash\n   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not\n   need their timestamps preserved.\n2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,\n   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.\n   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`\n   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls\n   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.\n\n---\n\n## 4. On-disk layout\n\nShared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may\nuse `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.\n\n```\n~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/\n├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time\n│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose\n├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends\n├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)\n└── hot-main/\n    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this\n    │   └── info\n    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main\n    ├── snapshots/\n    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    │   │   ├── STAMP\n    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build\n    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/\n    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink\n```\n\nSnapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse\nlexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`\ncalls and no name parsing.\n\n### `STAMP` schema\n\nA flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts\nparse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase\nhex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever\n`eval`ed or `source`d.\n\n```\nsha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>\nkeyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>\ntimestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>\ntimestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>\nstatus=complete|partial\nbuild_seconds=<integer>\ntoolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>\nsnapshot=<snapshot directory name>\nwarmer_version=1\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]\n                          [--targets \"<lake targets>\"] [--lock-timeout S]\n                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]\n```\n\n### 5.1 Writer lease\n\nAcquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic\ntest-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,\n`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.\n\nStaleness is decided in this order:\n\n* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead\n  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.\n* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).\n\nThe TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this\nrepository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,\n2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease\nmid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to\nprevent.\n\n**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that\nboth judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;\n`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and\nre-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A\n`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.\n\n### 5.2 Build\n\n1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`\n   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.\n   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and\n   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).\n2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).\n3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**\n   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and\n   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,\n   finish, then warm again.\n4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply\n   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.\n   **No `lake update`.**\n5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.\n   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is\n   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent\n   prompts may later read.\n\n### 5.3 Atomic publish\n\nThe publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:\n\n1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with\n   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the\n   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).\n2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.\n3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.\n   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already\n   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**\n4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over\n   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).\n\n> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,\n> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would\n> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real\n> trap, not a hypothetical one.\n\nConsumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the\nresolved concrete path for the rest of the run.\n\n### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional\n\nIf `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and\nexits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`\ncommit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did\ncompile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say\nso loudly.\n\nA non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *\"main did not build cleanly\"* —\nnot *\"nothing was published.\"* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a\nreason to retry.\n\n### 5.5 Retention\n\nKeep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's\n10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never\ncollected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has\nresolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging\ndirectories older than an hour are swept.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The consumer — `warm-worktree.sh`\n\n```\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh [<worktree>] [--force] [--build] [--no-build]\n                           [--force-cold] [--skip-packages] [--status]\n```\n\nThe consumer is **read-only with respect to the cache**. It refuses outright to\noperate on any path inside `hot-main/repo` or `hot-main/snapshots`.\n\nDecision procedure:\n\n1. Compute the worktree's own keyhash (§3).\n2. Resolve `current` **once**; require `build/` and `STAMP` to exist.\n3. Read and validate the `STAMP`. A malformed stamp is treated as *no snapshot*.\n4. **Keyhash gate.** Mismatch → warn with both hashes, name the likely cause\n   (toolchain / manifest / lakefile change), point at the warmer, and take the\n   cold path. Never a partial reuse, never a silent skip.\n5. **Warm path**: `cp -c -R <snapshot>/build → <worktree>/.lake/build.incoming.$$`,\n   then `rename` into place. Write the idempotency marker\n   `<worktree>/.lake/.mipstarre-warm-stamp` recording the snapshot name, keyhash,\n   snapshot status and time. Then fetch tier 2 with `lake exe cache get`.\n   No full build unless `--build` is given — the point of the warm path is that\n   the agent's next incremental `lake build` compiles only its own delta.\n6. **Cold path**: `lake exe cache get`, then a full `lake build` under the\n   machine-wide lock (§7), unless `--no-build`.\n\n### 6.1 Idempotency and the do-not-clobber rule\n\nRe-running on an already-warmed worktree is a no-op for tier 1. Specifically:\n\n* marker snapshot **and** keyhash both match the resolved snapshot → skip the\n  clone;\n* `.lake/build` is populated but was **not** warmed from this snapshot → leave it\n  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it\n  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.\n\n### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink\n\nOn APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near\ninstantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid\nfor only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a\n*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is\nprecisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or\nbind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations\nis the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Concurrency: two locks, deliberately separate\n\n| lock | path | held by | protects |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| writer lease | `hot-main/.writer-lease` | the warmer only | the snapshot store and `hot-main/repo` |\n| full-build lock | `.full-build-lock` | warmer **and** consumers | RAM/CPU: one full `lake build` machine-wide |\n\nThey are separate so that a consumer's own full build can proceed while the\nwarmer sits idle between commits, and so that a warmer holding the writer lease\ndoes not block a consumer that only wants to *read* a published snapshot.\n\n`DESIGN.md` #7: **single-file `lake env lean <file>` checks take no lock.** They\nare read-only over existing oleans, which is exactly why the `.githooks/pre-push`\ngate uses them per changed file rather than a whole-library build. Do not add\nlocking there.\n\nThe parent's equivalent constraint was runner disk exhaustion, severe enough that\na CI job dropped Lean setup entirely and now only emits a notice\n(`pr-ci.yml:314`). Locally the binding resource is RAM during a Mathlib-scale\nbuild; the lock is the analog of a concurrency group.\n\nBoth locks use the same mkdir/rename-to-break protocol described in §5.1, with\nthe same liveness-first staleness rule, so a consumer and the warmer agree on\nwhat a stale lock is.\n\n### 7.1 Interoperating with `local/bin/ci.sh`\n\n`ci.sh` takes the same machine-wide full-build lock around its build step. Two\ncompatibility hazards follow, and both are handled here:\n\n* **Path.** All four takers — `cache-warmer.sh`, `warm-worktree.sh`, `ci.sh`,\n  and `housekeeping.sh`'s linter sweep — default the lock to\n  **`$CACHE_ROOT/.full-build-lock`** and honour the override\n  **`MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK`**. One path, one mutex. (Historical note: the\n  first draft had `ci.sh` on `$CACHE_ROOT/hot-main/.full-build-lock` and the\n  sweep on a third flock — *two different paths are two independent mutexes,\n  and the invariant is silently void*; unified 2026-08-30, see\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.)\n* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO\n  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.\n  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude \"no pid, therefore\n  stale\" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here\n  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then\n  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`\n  field is read as \"this host\", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Fresh-worktree bootstrap — `worktree-setup.sh`\n\nReplaces `.codex/setup.sh` (the Codex cloud environment hook) per `DESIGN.md`'s\nGitHub→local mapping. Order of operations:\n\n1. **Assert `elan`** — never install it by piping a URL into a shell. This is a\n   developer machine, not a disposable runner. Missing `elan` is a hard, actionable\n   error.\n2. **PATH**: `$HOME/.elan/bin` is exported for this process. The shell rc file is\n   modified **only** under `--persist-path`; otherwise the line to add is printed.\n3. **Toolchain guard**: `elan toolchain install $(cat lean-toolchain)`, once, only\n   if the pin is not already installed.\n4. **No `lake update`** — stated in the log, not silently omitted (§2).\n5. **`origin/main` check** (`DESIGN.md` #8): a warning, because the hooks and every\n   diff-based audit silently self-disable without it. Silent self-disabling is the\n   documented failure this check exists to surface.\n6. **Fresh-state workaround** (§8.2).\n7. **`warm-worktree.sh`** — invoked from the copy *next to this script*, not the\n   copy inside the worktree being bootstrapped. A worktree may hold an unreviewed\n   branch; the bootstrap must not execute code from the tree it is bootstrapping.\n   This is the local analog of `DESIGN.md` #5 (trusted prompts come from `main`).\n   If the consumer script is missing, this is a **hard error**: without it the\n   worktree would start cold, silently, which is the outcome the whole protocol\n   exists to prevent.\n8. **`scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`**, then `--check`. `docs/ci-automation.md`\n   calls out `--check` specifically for *\"each fresh worktree used for a PR.\"*\n\n`--check` is report-only and mutates nothing (`DESIGN.md` #10). It exits non-zero\nif anything is missing.\n\n### 8.1 Git environment hygiene\n\nEvery invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in\n`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every\nvariable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a\nscript invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into\nLake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.\n\n### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround\n\nKept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a\npristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.\n\n*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib\npost-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before\nfetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not\nexist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create\nthe directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.\n\n*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is\n**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.\nRecorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed\nby a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts\ntherefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before\nfetching.\n\n`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete\ndownloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks\na checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from\nsource.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Telemetry\n\nEvery full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to\n`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.\n\n```jsonc\n{\"ts\": \"<ISO 8601 with offset>\",\n \"kind\": \"warm\" | \"rebuild\" | \"cache-get\",\n \"trigger\": \"<who asked for this>\",\n \"outcome\": \"success\" | \"failed\",\n \"seconds\": <int>,\n \"sha\": \"<commit, when known>\",\n \"note\": \"<sanitized, ≤400 chars>\"}\n```\n\n* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.\n* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).\n* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.\n\nThree properties are load-bearing:\n\n* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked\n  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the\n  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and\n  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.\n* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s\n  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every\n  failure path degrades to a warning.\n* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400\n  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is\n  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).\n\n---\n\n## 10. Operating procedures\n\n```bash\n# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main\n\n# What is published right now?\nlocal/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status\n\n# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis\n\n# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.\nlocal/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check\n\n# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force\n\n# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?\nlocal/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status\n```\n\nAfter a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm\nfirst, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot\nis invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run\n`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in\neach worktree serialized behind one lock.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades\n\n| condition | behaviour |\n|---|---|\n| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |\n| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |\n| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |\n| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |\n| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |\n| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |\n| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |\n| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |\n| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |\n| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |\n| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |\n| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Never a silent no-op.\n# Protocol: issues and pull requests\n\nNormative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in\n`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is\n`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for\nissues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*\nhere and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no\nshadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error\nfails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).\n\n## 1. Records, names, tools\n\nIssues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,\nno frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation\n(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the\nretired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the\nrepository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a\nlabel absent from GitHub is reported, never invented.\n`pr_open.py --issue N` inherits only its explicit descriptive-label allowlist\nfrom issue N, unions it with explicit `--label` values, and adds those labels\nwithout removing existing PR labels. Scheduling, approval and owner-state\nlabels are never inherited. Before push, creation/adoption requires at least\none descriptive label, supplied explicitly, inherited, or already on the PR;\notherwise the command explains how the operator can classify the change.\nGitHub still validates label existence; the allowlist is an inheritance policy,\nnot a replacement registry. Backfills use the same additive API and inspect\nthe actual change when the source issue itself is unlabeled. Briefs (the design record\nper issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.\n\nPrerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**\n(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.\nThe edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.\nA prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The\n\"Dependencies\" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never\nthe record. The command first\nreads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous\nfailure; it is therefore safe to repeat. It runs that checkout's `.githooks/pre-push` against the exact\nref tuple before starting `receive-pack`, then pushes the captured commit under\nan exact remote-tip lease.  The native hook performs a short defense-in-depth\ncomparison when selected, while the helper's lease makes a moved remote ref fail\nclosed even when that hook is stale or absent. When an explicitly\nrequested/default main push succeeded and the snapshot created a new telemetry\ncommit, it checked-pushes main once more without creating another snapshot.\nBranch-only calls never implicitly publish main. Evidence contracts\n\nAll evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).\n\n**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one\n`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,\n`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,\n`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.\n`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`\nafter it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads\nthe *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined\nstatus, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one\nPR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by\n`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.\n\n**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,\ncarrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the\nline `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.\nUnchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\\s*[-*]\\s*\\[ \\]`; clean means\n`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. See rem:linearity-import.\n\\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test~\\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}]\n\t\\label{thm:linearity}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable, MIPStarRE.QPBT.stateDepDistSq}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables}\n\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables_binaryObservableDistSq}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{def:povm-conventions, lem:binary-measurement-distance}\n\tLet $t$ be a positive integer and $\\delta \\ge 0$. Let $\\rho$ be a\n\tdensity operator on a Hilbert space $\\hilb$ and let\n\t$\\{\\mathcal{O}^u\\}$ be a set of binary observables indexed by\n\t$u \\in \\F_2^t$ acting on $\\hilb$, such that on average over $u, u'$\n\tchosen uniformly at random from $\\F_2^t$,\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\E_{u,u'} \\Re \\Tr\\big(\\mathcal{O}^u \\, \\mathcal{O}^{u'} \\,\n\t\t\\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \\, \\rho\\big) \\ge 1 - \\delta\\,.\n\t\\]\n\tThen there exist a Hilbert space $\\hilb'$, a pure state\n\t$\\ket{\\mathrm{anc}} \\in \\hilb'$, and binary observables\n\t$\\{\\mathcal{L}^u\\}$ indexed by $u \\in \\F_2^t$ acting on\n\t$\\hilb \\ot \\hilb'$ such that, writing\n\t$\\rho' = \\rho \\ot \\ket{\\mathrm{anc}}\\bra{\\mathrm{anc}}$, the exact\n\tlinearity\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\mathcal{L}^u \\, \\mathcal{L}^{u'} = \\mathcal{L}^{u+u'}\n\t\\]\n\tholds for all $u, u' \\in \\F_2^t$, and\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\E_{u} \\, d_{\\rho'}\\big(\\mathcal{L}^u,\\ \\mathcal{O}^u \\ot\n\t\t\\Id_{\\hilb'}\\big)^2 \\le 2\\delta\\,,\n\t\\]\n\twhere the expectation is over $u$ chosen uniformly at random from\n\t$\\F_2^t$ and\n\t$d_{\\sigma}(S,T)\n\t= \\big(\\Tr\\big((S-T)^\\dagger (S-T)\\, \\sigma\\big)\\big)^{1/2}$\n\tdenotes the state-dependent distance with respect to a density\n\toperator $\\sigma$. Equivalently, in the distance $d^{\\mathrm{bin}}_\\sigma$\n\tbetween the binary projective measurements associated with the\n\tobservables (Lemma~\\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}),\n\t\\[\n\t\t\\E_{u} \\, d^{\\mathrm{bin}}_{\\rho'}\\big(\\mathcal{L}^u,\\\n\t\t\\mathcal{O}^u \\ot \\Id_{\\hilb'}\\big)^2 \\le \\delta\\,.\n\t\\]\n\tThe cited source prints the first bound with $\\delta$ in place of\n\t$2\\delta$; that normalization is false, and the bounds stated here are\n\tthe ones its argument establishes\n\t(Remark~\\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}).\n\\end{theorem}\n\\begin{proof}\n\t\\leanok\n\t\\uses{lem:binary-measurement-distance, lem:blr-defect-identity,\n\t\tlem:boolean-representation-stability}\n\tThis is Theorem~10 of Natarajan and Vidick~\\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity},\n\twhose Fourier--Naimark argument is followed; \\cite{Ji2020MIPStar} invokes\n\tthe result without proof. Write $\\chi_v(u) = (-1)^{v \\cdot u}$ and\n\t$\\widehat{\\mathcal{O}}^v = \\E_u \\, \\chi_v(u) \\, \\mathcal{O}^u$ as in\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.\n\n\t\\emph{From the correlation to the multiplicative defect.} For\n\t$u, u' \\in \\F_2^t$, expanding\n\t$(\\mathcal{O}^u \\mathcal{O}^{u'} - \\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^\\dagger\n\t(\\mathcal{O}^u \\mathcal{O}^{u'} - \\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})$ with\n\t$(\\mathcal{O}^w)^2 = \\Id$ and $\\Tr \\rho = 1$, as in the proof of\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}, gives\n\t\\[\n\t\td_\\rho\\big(\\mathcal{O}^u \\mathcal{O}^{u'}, \\mathcal{O}^{u+u'}\\big)^2\n\t\t= 2 - 2 \\Re \\Tr\\big(\\mathcal{O}^{u'} \\mathcal{O}^u\n\t\t\\mathcal{O}^{u'+u} \\rho\\big)\\,,\n\t\\]\n\tthe two cross terms being adjoint to each other. Exchanging the two\n\tcoordinates of the uniform pair $(u,u')$, the hypothesis yields\n\t$\\E_{u,u'} d_\\rho(\\mathcal{O}^u \\mathcal{O}^{u'},\n\t\\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \\le 2\\delta$. No commutation among the\n\tobservables is used.\n\n\t\\emph{The Fourier-square measurement and its Naimark rounding.} By\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} the operators\n\t$B^v = (\\widehat{\\mathcal{O}}^v)^2$ are positive semidefinite and sum to\n\t$\\Id$, so they form a POVM indexed by $\\F_2^t$.\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:naimark-helper}, applied with an ancillary space $\\hilb'$\n\tof dimension $2^t + 1$ and with $\\ket{\\mathrm{anc}}$ the basis vector of\n\tits extra direction, produces orthogonal projectors on $\\hilb \\ot \\hilb'$\n\tcompressing along $\\ket{\\mathrm{anc}}$ to the $B^v$; the residual\n\tprojector of the construction is folded into the outcome $v = 0$, which\n\tgives a projective measurement $\\{C^v\\}$ resolving the identity on\n\t$\\hilb \\ot \\hilb'$ whose compression is still $\\{B^v\\}$, because the\n\t$B^v$ themselves sum to $\\Id$. The measurement\n\tform follows by halving, through the normalization identity of\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}.\n\n\tThe obligations attached to the theorem at its point of use --- the\n\tcorrespondence between the correlation hypothesis above and the relation\n\t$\\approx_\\delta$ of Definition~\\ref{def:povm-distance}, the\n\tinstantiation of $\\rho$ as a reduced state of $\\ket{\\hat\\psi}$, the\n\tabsorption of the ancilla register into padding of the strategy state,\n\tand the identity $\\mathcal{L}^0 = \\Id$ --- are enumerated in\n\tRemark~\\ref{rem:linearity-import} and addressed in the proof of\n\tLemma~\\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]\n\t\\label{rem:linearity-import}\n\tTheorem~\\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form established by the\n\targument of \\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, with the normalization of its\n\tdistance bound corrected as described in\n\tRemark~\\ref{rem:linearity-distance-normalization}. ## Project Overview

This repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics
around $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of
[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is
the **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active
track is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\*=RE*

CI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and
merges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through
`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before
doing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the

  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source

- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint

- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer

A legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.

**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):

## Faithful Formalization Policy

A declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean
statement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.
Changing a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in
`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a
faithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.
This applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper
result, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the
hypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose
conclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra
load-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not
the paper theorem.
The project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize
them as permanent infrastructure.

If the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must
not mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either
leave the source-labelled entry without `\leanok`, or state the restricted or
conditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are
displayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\leanok` only
against a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must
not be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.

When a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a
source theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.
The note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of
the cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,
deriving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.

This rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as
`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked
from the blueprint by `\lean{...}` and `\leanok`.

Before editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,
`prop:*`):

1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.
2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are
   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.
3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer
   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary
   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.
4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named
   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.
5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A
   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it
   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains
   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem
   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its
   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like
   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example
   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a
   name ending in `_ofObligations`.
6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper
   with `\leanok`.

When reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package
hypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction
and turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not
actually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as
a strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave
the missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a
tracked `sorry` during a repair PR.

Some side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a
division, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model
instances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of
assumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and
documented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is
different: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such
as a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,
`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the
paper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions
should not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;
they require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.

These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.

1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green

   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.

   unset means enabled.

6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies
   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,
   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.
7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);
   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.
8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently
   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a
   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.
9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid

11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization

    start, end, wall_s, usage: {input, cached_input, cache_write, output, reasoning},
    exit, dispatcher, worktree, status: active|done|failed|archived}`
  Written only by `local/bin/dispatch.sh` / `telemetry.py`. New dispatches always
  supply `account` (`primary` or `second`) and the exact resolved `model`
  passed to the CLI (environment override, otherwise selected-account config).
  External rows use allocator accounts `primary|second`; native rows use the
  active key label (`space` or historical `relay-1`) in both `account` and
  `key_label`, with `dispatcher: native`.
  When the dispatcher supplies a reasoning override, `requested_effort` is its
  effective value after model-specific normalization. It records the CLI request,
  not provider-measured effort. All three fields remain optional for historical
  rows and legacy replay callers.
- `results/telemetry/owner-sessions.jsonl` —
  `{name, role, model, issue, pr?, worktree?, base?, start, end?, wall_s?,
    status, tokens?, tool_uses?, findings_fixed?, commits?, note?}`.
  Written only by the owner session and `/tmp/claude-lane-prep.sh` /
  `/tmp/claude-lane-finish.sh`; `tokens` is the harness-reported subagent total.
  For `role: mathfix`, `issue` identifies the gap whose shared budget is charged.
- `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl` —
  `{ts, kind: warm|rebuild|cache-get|ci-build, trigger, seconds, outcome,
    sha?, note?}`
- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated bullets; free prose; one incident per
  bullet: symptom → diagnosis → fix → lesson.

Duties:

- **Every external Codex session goes through `dispatch.sh`** so token usage and wall
  time land in `sessions.jsonl`. A session started any other way is a
  telemetry hole; if one happens, backfill a line with `dispatcher: manual`.
- Historical native descendants were recorded with `telemetry.py native-record`
  under `sessions.md`:
  `dispatcher: native`, root/parent IDs, key label, actual model/requested effort,
  worktree, timestamps and status. `observed_usage` preserves raw cumulative rollout
  counters, but `usage` remains null with `usage_scope: unknown`; parent inclusion
  of descendants is unverified. Never convert missing usage to zero or sum these
  observations. Private homes and credential data are not serialized. Requested
  CLI Ultra is distinct from wire/returned Max seen in owner migration receipts;
  absent request-specific wire evidence stays null, not inferred from configuration.
- **Every full build** (warmer, CI, cold rebuild) lands in `builds.jsonl`.
- **Stage transitions** are logged by the orchestrator (main session) at the
  moment they happen, not reconstructed later.
- Claude-side (non-Codex) subagent fleets are recorded in
  `owner-sessions.jsonl` and summarized into `stages.jsonl` as `milestone`
  entries with token totals, since they bypass `dispatch.sh`.

## Research-data invariants

Model-policy records (#301) retain `requested_model`, `selected_model`,
`effective_model` only when observed, `job_class`, and `model_policy` with
routine/hard classification and the explicit hardness/escalation rationale.
External capture without model evidence records effective model as null, not the
CLI argument. Historical native observations retain all bound current-turn contexts; mixed
models/efforts and requested/observed mismatches fail closed. Prior/forked contexts
are not attributed to a new job. Requested effort remains distinct from provider
effort; missing usage remains unknown and historical records are not rewritten.
`dispatch_kind` is new/resume/grandfathered; `activation_at` fixes the accounting
boundary. Ratio reports count actual distinct new threads with matching observed
and selected models, with a rolling 100-dispatch window and separate cumulative
counts. Unknowns may resolve from later observations; conflicts remain unknown.
Main, pre-activation workers and resumes do not count. Preserve predecessor and
cumulative-budget links recorded when a model change required a fresh native identity.

The project doubles as a study of a self-evolving formalization workflow.
Three artifacts must therefore stay trustworthy:

- `EVOLUTION.md` — complete: every protocol change has an entry.
- `events.md` — honest: failures are recorded as failures, including agent
  mistakes, wasted builds, and reverted work.
- `sessions.jsonl` + `stages.jsonl` — quantitative: per-stage cost
  (time, tokens, session counts) reconstructible by a script, not by memory.

This directory is the operative workflow of the repository: the local
replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and
invariants: [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md). Protocol changes: follow
[`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md).

## The lifecycle at a glance

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
```

1. **File an issue**: `local/bin/issue_new.py --title "..." --body-file b.md --label ...` opens
   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
   sub-issue. Record each prerequisite, including one already closed, with
   `local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`; the command is
   safe to repeat. The brief for the issue goes in `local/briefs/`.
2. **Open a PR**: create branch `issue-<number>-slug`, worktree under
   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),
   which pushes the branch and opens the GitHub PR.
3. **Dispatch agents**: only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover
   --issue NNNN --worktree .worktrees/<name> -- "task"`. Session telemetry
   lands in `results/telemetry/`. Lease-backed native descendants are retired;
   `protocols/sessions.md` retains their history separately.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

**Choosing the next packet.** `local/bin/ready_packets.py` walks the packet tree
under the Stage 4.3 tracker #47 — chapter trackers, their packets, and nested
chains such as Magic Square rigidity — and prints the open leaf packets whose
GitHub issue dependencies (`blocked_by`) are all closed. `--all` adds the
blocked packets with their open blockers, `--json` feeds the lane launcher, and
`--root N` restricts the walk to one tracker. Prerequisites live in those edges
only: the "Dependencies" bullets in a packet body are commentary
(`protocols/issues-prs.md` §1). A merged packet closes its issue and therefore
unblocks its dependents with no edit anywhere.

## Telemetry

Retired useful-work queue: [historical protocol](protocols/useful-queue.md).

Session, stage, build, and incident records live under `results/telemetry/` as
described in [`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md). The
[`design-decisions.md`](../results/telemetry/design-decisions.md) register is
the short, chronological index of owner and operator choices that shaped the
workflow; each row points to the longer primary record. Record reasoning in the
pointed event or owner log rather than expanding the index into a second log.

## Ground rules for agents

- Read `AGENTS.md` first; the faithfulness policy and proof-integrity
  blockers are unchanged from the parent project.
- Never run `lake update`. Never write to the hot cache. Full `lake build`
  goes through the machine-wide lock (`warm-worktree.sh`/`ci.sh` handle it).
- Publish branches through `checked-push.sh` (used internally by `pr_open.py`,
  `github-sync.sh`, and `autofix.sh`) so the gate finishes before push transport
  starts.
- One session never reviews its own diff.
- Worker sessions use `dispatch.sh`; the native lease and review transport in
  `sessions.md` are historical and must not be used for new work.
- Invoke workflow tools through the primary checkout's path
  (`/…/MIPStarRE-dev/local/bin/…`), never through a worktree's copy — a
  branch's copy can predate protocol fixes (EVOLUTION.md, 2026-08-30).
- After merging `main` or a stack parent, preserve every incoming-only path.
  The reference-transaction hook checks the exact merge object before the
  branch ref moves, while the pre-commit hook checks the pending index when a
  merge is committed later. Both run `local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py`.
  `merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit HEAD` audits a merge already
  committed by a lane whose branch copy predates the hooks.
- Friction with any protocol → log it in `results/telemetry/events.md`;
  propose amendments per `protocols/meta.md`.

## Declaring a track finished

The end of a track is gated like every other step of the lifecycle.
[`protocols/completion.md`](protocols/completion.md) is the definition of done
— zero proof debt, a built axiom audit over the headline theorems, terminal
paper-gap rows, marked or explicitly exempted blueprint nodes, a comparator
challenge pinned to an ancestor commit and naming every headline theorem,
truthful status docs, and the files an ITP artifact submission needs — and
`scripts/completion_gate.py check --track <track>` is the model-free checker
that decides the mechanically checkable part of it. No completion statement,
umbrella-issue closure or release tag without a passing run on the exact
commit. The gate is intentionally outside the blocking PR CI.
